Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick updates over the weekend. Our security team needs a short, formal statement from Redwood confirming that, following the 2027-04-22 service incident, there is no evidence of customer-data exfiltration or unauthorized access to Acme records. Specifically we'd like:

- A concise statement we can include in our internal incident report that affirms no customer PII or transaction records were exported.
- A short description of the log checks performed (time windows sampled, hash reconciliation, tools used).
- Any attachments with the evidence summary (hash report, sample logs).

We need to close our internal ticket by EOD Pacific. Can you provide this by 2 PM PT?

Appreciate it —
Maya Singh

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence of no-data-exfiltration from 2027-04-22 incident

Karthik / Stephanie —

I've completed the checks and prepared the artifacts. Summary of actions performed (technical detail for your records):

1) Time window sampled: 2027-04-22 03:30:00 — 04:30:00 UTC (includes the observed incident window).
2) Hosts/streams inspected: inference-gpu-pool-1 (k8s nodes), request-router-02, outbound egress proxy logs, object-store write-audit logs.
3) Methods: prefix-based log sampling using log-iterator v1.4; MD5/SHA256 reconciliation against immutable audit index; search for tenant IDs: acct-acme-*, transaction ids with pattern TX-.
4) Findings: No outbound connections containing object payloads matching Acme tenant IDs. No successful write operations to external buckets with Acme object hashes. Hash reconciliation: all stored hashes present in audit index; no mismatches.

Artifacts attached:
- log-hash-summary-20270425.pdf (one-page reconciliation table; includes SHA256 digest list)
- access-log-snippet-20270422.txt (redacted lines showing request IDs and host timestamps)

Draft language suggestion to provide to customer:  
"Redwood Inference conducted targeted log sampling across compute hosts and egress points for the time period surrounding the 2027-04-22 incident. Reconciliation of stored object hashes and audit indices shows no evidence of customer records being exported or copied to external destinations. We found no indications of unauthorized access to Acme Payments tenant records during the sampled window."

If that wording looks good, Stephanie — feel free to refine for tone and send. I also included MD5/SHA256 summaries in the PDF for their audit team.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Security Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Formal confirmation: log integrity & absence of customer-data exfiltration

Maya and Acme security team —

Per your request, please find below Redwood Inference's formal confirmation regarding the 2027-04-22 incident. Attached: log-hash-summary-20270425.pdf and access-log-snippet-20270422.txt.

Statement (for your incident report):
Redwood Inference conducted a targeted forensic review of activity associated with the 2027-04-22 service incident. The investigation included:
- Sampling and inspection of compute host logs and request-router traces for 2027-04-22 03:30:00 — 04:30:00 UTC.
- Reconciliation of object storage hashes (SHA256) with Redwood's immutable audit index.
- Examination of egress proxy logs and object-store write-audit trails for outbound data transfers.

Result: Our review found no evidence that Acme Payments customer data or transaction records were accessed and exported to external destinations. Hash reconciliation between stored objects and the audit index produced no mismatches for objects associated with Acme tenant identifiers. The attached PDF contains the reconciliation table and hash digests; the attached text file includes redacted log snippets showing request IDs and timestamps used for validation.

Scope notes and caveats:
- The conclusion applies to the sampled time window above and to the systems and audit trails described.
- We performed prefix/tenant-based searches and cryptographic hash reconciliation; while sampling covers the incident window, a broader full-historical scan can be performed on request.

If you need additional artifacts (full egress captures, extended time-range scans, or notarized chain-of-custody documentation), let us know and we will prioritize.

Requested next step: please confirm if this statement and the attached artifacts meet your needs for closure, or share any specific phrasing you require for the Acme internal report.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sales Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
